speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To narrow this down, have you noticed any recent fevers or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; have you noticed any specific changes in your stool, such as black, tarry stools or blood, and do you have a history of blood cancers or autoimmune disorders? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal blood work, could you tell me if your abdominal pain is specifically located in the right lower quadrant, and have you noticed any skin rashes or changes in your skin color? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT_Scan

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma with possible secondary involvement. The combination of "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and a fixed neck mass is highly suggestive of lymphoma despite the normal CBC. I recommend an urgent biopsy of the enlarged lymph node and a PET-CT scan for staging.
